Task.title: Task
Task.description: Represents a task in the TaskTrack Budget application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Task entity.

dueDate.description: The due date for the task.

frequency.description: Frequency of the task (daily, weekly, monthly).

completed.description: Indicates whether the task is completed or not.

definition.description: Stores tasks associated with a specific user. Path-based ownership enables simple security rules based on `request.auth.uid`. The `userId` path parameter represents the unique ID of the user, and the `taskId` path parameter represents the unique ID of the task.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user.

params.name: taskId
params.description: The unique identifier of the task.

firestore.reasoning: The data structure is designed to store tasks for a task tracking application named "TaskTrack Budget". The structure prioritizes authorization independence by storing tasks under a user-specific path, `/users/{userId}/tasks/{taskId}`. This eliminates the need for complex security rules involving `get()` calls to parent documents, ensuring atomic operations and easier debugging.  Since tasks are owned by individual users, there is no need for denormalized data to manage shared access or team-based permissions. The structure is segregated by storing all tasks within a specific user's document, enabling simple ownership-based security rules.  This structure supports secure list operations (QAPs) as Firestore rules can easily filter tasks based on the `userId` in the path.
